notes: Sourced from Wisycom's own MPR50-IEM User Manual (Rev.06, FW v1.7, dated 14 June 2024), hosted at wisycom.com — the dedicated wisycom.com/products/mpr50-iem/ product page itself renders no spec content client-side, so the official downloadable manual PDF was used instead. The MPR50-IEM is a battery-powered belt-pack true-diversity IEM receiver, not a rack device (no rackUnits). Two RF hardware variants exist with identical connectors, differing only in tuning range: MPR50-IEM-N (470-700MHz) and MPR50-IEM-M (566-798MHz). No connector in the given list matches the actual SMA antenna jacks, so BNC was used as the closest coax RF approximation per instructions — do not treat this as literal BNC hardware. No grade was set on any port: antenna ports are RF (not SDI video), the headphone jack is analog, and USB/IR speeds are unspecified. There is no standalone DC power jack on the unit itself; power comes from user-replaceable/rechargeable AA or proprietary lithium batteries (2xAA, MPRLBP, Ricoh DB-50, or DR9708), charged via the integrated Micro-USB-B port or an external dedicated charger cradle (not a body connector). An optional external "ADTMPR" 9-18VDC power adapter accessory (pigtail/XLR-4F/Hirose-4F variants) exists for the MPR30/MPR50 product family but is a separate accessory, not a connector built into the MPR50-IEM body, so it was not included as a port. Product "type" was set to the closest available enum value, "Wireless mic" — the catalog has no dedicated "IEM receiver" type; this device actually receives (not transmits) wireless in-ear-monitor audio.

ports.name: Antenna A
ports.note: RF diversity antenna input; physical connector is SMA (threaded), which is not in the allowed connector list — BNC chosen as closest coax RF analog.

ports.name: Antenna B
ports.note: RF diversity antenna input (second diversity branch); physical connector is SMA, approximated as BNC (see Antenna A note).

ports.name: Headphone Output
ports.note: Lockable 3.5mm stereo jack (TRS). Tip=Left(hot), Ring=Right(hot), Sleeve=Gnd. Max output power 2x100mW @ 32Ω (peak headroom +23dBm/200mW).

ports.name: Micro-USB-B
ports.note: Integrated port used both for onboard charging of lithium battery and for wired configuration/firmware update via Wisycom Manager PC application; USB speed not specified in manual.

ports.name: Infrared (IR)
ports.note: Front-panel IR window used for wireless sync with a Wisycom transmitter and for setup/firmware programming via optional UPKmini IR-to-USB interface.
